Find the most frequently repeated triplets across participants

find_frequent_triplets.Rd

Given a list of per-participant triplet data frames, finds the triplets judged by the largest number of distinct participants, treating a triplet as the same trial regardless of which option appeared on the left or the right (but not regardless of which item was the reference/Center item – that's a different question being asked, not the same trial mirrored).

Usage

find_frequent_triplets(
  triplet_list,
  n = 50,
  min_participants = 1,
  exclude_check = TRUE
)

Arguments

triplet_list

Named list of per-participant triplet data frames (the package's standard Center/Left/Right/Answer/ worker_id shape, e.g. icon_triplets).

n

Integer. Number of triplets to return, ranked by the number of distinct participants who judged them (ties broken by total trial count, then alphabetically by the triplet's own name – see Details). Default 50.

min_participants

Integer. Only triplets judged by at least this many distinct participants are eligible to be returned, even if fewer than n such triplets exist. Default 1 (no filtering).

exclude_check

Logical. Drop sampleAlg == "check" rows (attention-check trials) before counting, if a sampleAlg column is present. Default TRUE.

Value

A data frame with one row per selected triplet, sorted by decreasing frequency, with columns:

triplet

The triplet's unique code, from make.tripnames (Center_Left_Right, with Left/Right in a fixed, left/right-independent order).

Center, Left, Right

The triplet's items, in the format test.model/get.hoacc expect – so the result can be used directly as (or merged into) a Center/Left/Right/Answer-shaped triplet data frame once an Answer is assigned (e.g. a majority vote, the same way make.vmat computes one for genuine validation trials).

n_participants

Number of distinct participants (by worker_id) who judged this triplet at least once.

n_trials

Total number of trials judging this triplet, pooled across all participants – can exceed n_participants if any one participant judged the same triplet more than once.

Details

This is for retrofitting a post-hoc validation set onto legacy data collected before this package's sampleAlg == "validation" convention existed, where every triplet was instead sampled independently at random for each participant. Because triplets are drawn from a combinatorially large pool (an m-item study has m * choose(m - 1, 2) distinct Center/{Left, Right} combinations), real cross-participant overlap is only likely to turn up when m is small and/or the number of trials per participant is large relative to that pool – check that n_participants actually reaches a usable minimum for the top triplets returned here before treating them as a real validation set, rather than assuming it from the item count alone.

Once a usable set of frequent triplets is found, a natural next step is to compute each one's majority-vote answer across the participants who judged it (the same construction make.vmat uses for genuine validation trials) and treat that as its Answer for a held-out evaluation set. This function only finds and counts the candidate triplets – it does not compute majority votes itself, since doing so meaningfully requires first deciding on a frequency/participant threshold using the counts returned here.

Triplet identity is determined by make.tripnames, the same convention make.vmat uses for genuine validation trials: two trials are the same triplet if they share the same Center and the same unordered pair of Left/Right items. A trial with the same three items but a different Center is a different question (a different reference item), not the same triplet mirrored, and is counted separately.

Examples

freq <- find_frequent_triplets(icon_triplets, n = 10)
freq
#>              triplet Center  Left Right n_participants n_trials
#> 1  fdmob_fdfow_pnhob  fdmob fdfow pnhob              5        5
#> 2  fdmob_fdmow_fdmyb  fdmob fdmow fdmyb              5        5
#> 3  fdmow_fdmyw_fnfyw  fdmow fdmyw fnfyw              5        5
#> 4  fdmow_fnmyw_pdhnb  fdmow fnmyw pdhnb              5        5
#> 5  fdmyb_fdfob_pdhos  fdmyb fdfob pdhos              5        5
#> 6  fdmyb_fnfyb_pdcns  fdmyb fnfyb pdcns              5        5
#> 7  fnfyb_fdmyb_pdcnb  fnfyb fdmyb pdcnb              5        5
#> 8  fnmob_fdmob_fnmyb  fnmob fdmob fnmyb              5        5
#> 9  fnmyb_fdfob_pdcns  fnmyb fdfob pdcns              5        5
#> 10 fnmyb_pnhnb_pnhos  fnmyb pnhnb pnhos              5        5
